Subject: Clarify streaming vs polling SLA (TTFT + tokens/sec) for POC

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Quick follow-up from our infra team: we're evaluating a hybrid ingestion pattern where some clients will use a high-burst streaming integration (Server->Redwood->client) and others will poll a non-streaming endpoint. Before we finalize the POC scope, they need clarity on two things:

- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) expectations for streaming endpoints vs polling endpoints (95th/99th percentile windows).
- Sustained tokens/sec expectations and how these change under short bursts (30s-2min windows).

CloudFin is particularly sensitive to visible first-byte latency in our UI; the PM wants an SLA carveout if the streaming TTFT isn't comparable to polling. We also need to understand whether an exception or amendment is required for the Dedicated offering vs hosted API.

Can you point us to precise numbers and the path to get a temporary SLA carveout for our POC? If helpful, loop in whoever owns Dedicated capacity.

Thanks,
Natalie Park

Hi Natalie — great question and totally reasonable to get this nailed down before the POC. Short answer up-front:

- Polling (sync) endpoints: typical TTFT 40-120ms p95 on hosted API under normal load; sustained token throughput depends on endpoint config and batching.
- Streaming endpoints: TTFT can be dominated by request setup and first-chunk generation; typical TTFT p95 80-250ms on hosted API, but bursts and cold KV cache can push this higher.

That variance is why customers often request a carveout when they need comparable TTFT across modes. For the POC we can offer a limited exception tied to reserved capacity (Dedicated) + a short-term SLA amendment. I've attached a proposed SLA-waiver template and a short capacity estimate workbook so your infra can stress-test.

Can you confirm the expected concurrent streaming connections and the 30s/2min burst profile you mentioned? Once I have that, I'll loop in Karthik (engineering) for capacity and tradeoffs and Marissa will draft the commercial amendment.

Next steps (proposed):
- You send the burst profile + expected concurrency.
- Our eng team replies with adjusted TTFT and tokens/sec SLOs for Dedicated vs Hosted.
- We produce a one-page amendment and a DocuSign-ready waiver for the POC window.

Cheers,

Marissa / Diego — quick engineering take: the numbers in Marissa's suggested phrasing are reasonable for Dedicated with a warm KV cache and pre-provisioned burst capacity. Details and caveats: 

- TTFT: p95 <= 200ms is achievable if the rider conditions are met (dedicated warm instances, connection pre-warm, and limited model context length <= 1024 tokens). For hosted shared API we should not promise p95 <= 200ms during large multi-tenant bursts; estimate p95 250-500ms under noisy neighbor conditions.

- Sustained tokens/sec: 80 tokens/sec per connection average over 60s is fine for medium-size models (<= 7B FP16). For larger models or quantized variants we should adjust down to 50-60 tokens/sec.

- Burst handling: we recommend an explicit fallback policy — when sustained aggregate token demand exceeds provisioned burst capacity by >20% for more than 30s, we will: 1) gracefully degrade to a compatible quantized variant, or 2) shift connections to pre-warmed dedicated pool (if available).

If CloudFin accepts Dedicated for the POC and agrees to the pre-warm checklist (attached), we can commit to the waiver language Marissa proposed. Otherwise, we should set more conservative TTFT targets for hosted.

—Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime

Hi Natalie / Jason — thanks for the quick turn. Per our internal review (below), here's a consolidated POC proposal: 

1) Environment: Dedicated reserved pool (pre-warmed), 30-day POC window.
2) TTFT / throughput targets for POC: TTFT p95 <= 200ms for streaming connections; sustained tokens/sec 80 tokens/sec per connection averaged over 60s (applies to 7B-class models). Hosted API targets will be listed as best-effort with higher percentiles.
3) Fallbacks & remediation: If aggregate demand exceeds provisioned burst capacity by >20% for >30s, Redwood will (a) migrate traffic to a compatible quantized variant or (b) enact the fallback routing to the pre-warmed pool. If targets are missed more than 3x in a 7-day window, CloudFin is eligible for a remediation credit up to 10% of POC charges and Redwood will provide a prioritized RCA.

- Natalie: confirm concurrency and the expected burst shape (requests/min across the 30s and 2min windows).
